column19: Description DeFi yield aggregator where vaults allocate deposited assets into programmatic strategies across underlying protocols to optimize risk-adjusted returns. (yearn.fi) Yield optimizer whose vaults deploy deposits into external liquidity pools/farms and automatically compound rewards back into principal assets. (docs.beefy.finance) Yield aggregator where vault deposits are deployed into third-party DeFi protocols via strategies to generate yield that is shared with depositors. (Harvest Finance) Protocol that tokenizes yield by splitting yield-bearing assets into PT (principal) and YT (yield) and provides AMMs for trading those exposures. (docs.pendle.finance) Protocol that created fixed/variable yield markets by splitting a yield-bearing asset into PT (principal) redeemable at maturity and YT (yield) capturing the yield component. (Delv Documentation) Protocol that enables fixed-rate, fixed-term lending by minting/trading fCash claims redeemable at maturity; fixed yield emerges from the discount/premium of fCash vs cash. (docs.notional.finance) Structured products vaults that automate systematic options strategies (e.g., selling OTM options) to generate yield. (docs.ribbon.finance) Structured DeFi product suite (SMART Yield) that packages underlying protocol yields into bond/tranche-like instruments. (lexology.com) Yield automation protocol offering (a) best-yield allocation and (b) tranche products that split risk/return into senior and junior classes. (docs.idle.finance)

(Harvest Finance) Fits criteria: transforms yield exposure (fixed/variable) and depends on multi-protocol yield sources + programmatic tokenization/market logic. (Delv Documentation) Included only for the yield-structuring component: it transforms yield into a term structure (fixed-rate markets) rather than simply sourcing yield from one primitive. (docs.notional.finance) Fits criteria: yield is engineered and transformed via strategy logic (options-selling) rather than sourced from a single primitive. (docs.ribbon.finance) Fits criteria: yield depends on multi-protocol aggregation and structured payoff logic, not a single primitive. (CoinGecko) Fits criteria: abstracts yield across protocols and transforms exposure via tranching (risk-adjusted yield products). (docs.idle.finance)
column21: Practitioner’s Note Diligence checklist: (1) which upstream protocols the vault touches, (2) strategy upgrade/admin controls, (3) keeper dependencies, (4) withdrawal liquidity assumptions under stress, (5) smart-contract/audit coverage per vault version (v2 vs v3). (docs.yearn.fi) Diligence checklist: (1) strategy contract risk (each vault is a different strategy), (2) reward token swap-path slippage/MEV, (3) upstream protocol risk (Curve/Convex/DEX LPs), (4) chain-bridge considerations if allocating cross-chain, (5) TVL concentration by a few flagship vaults. (docs.beefy.finance) Diligence checklist: (1) per-vault strategy complexity, (2) reliance on Curve/LP mechanics (historically relevant), (3) upgrade/timelock and admin controls, (4) withdrawal assumptions under stress, (5) post-incident security posture and audits. (Least Authority) Diligence checklist: (1) maturity and implied rate curve behavior, (2) oracle/market pricing assumptions for PT/YT, (3) liquidity depth around maturity, (4) underlying yield source risk (what generates the yield), (5) incentive/governance concentration risk. (docs.pendle.finance) Diligence checklist: (1) maturity/term risk, (2) PT discount mechanics (fixed rate only if PT bought at discount), (3) liquidity depth in PT markets, (4) underlying yield asset assumptions. (Delv Documentation) Boundary caution: Notional sits near Lending Markets. Classify here when your analysis is about rate curve / maturity markets (fCash) and yield transformation; classify in Lending when focusing on credit creation and collateral rules. (docs.notional.finance) Diligence checklist: (1) strategy payoff under spot/vol regime shifts, (2) vault parameter/upgrade controls, (3) settlement/oracle upgrade risk, (4) liquidity/withdrawal mechanics by epoch, (5) tail-risk events (vault drains / contract issues). (theblock.co) Risk flags dominate: (1) regulatory enforcement precedent (SEC), (2) governance/ops centralization risk, (3) underlying venue concentration, (4) product run-off / deprecation risk, (5) liquidity/exit constraints for bond-like products. (lexology.com) Diligence checklist: (1) what the tranche’s underlying strategy venue is, (2) coverage mechanics (how junior absorbs losses), (3) concentration in a single underlying market, (4) oracle/venue liquidation behavior, (5) governance/upgrade controls. (docs.idle.finance)
